text:
Predicates:
DeadlyDisease(x) ::: x is a deadly disease.
LowSurvivalRate(x) ::: x comes with a low survival rate.
SevereCancer(x) ::: x is a severe cancer.
BileDuctCancer(x) ::: x is bile duct cancer.
Cholangiocarcinoma(x) ::: x is Cholangiocarcinoma.
MildFlu(x) ::: x is mild flu.
ColorectalCancer(x) ::: x is colorectal cancer.
Form(x, y) ::: x is a form of y.

Premises:
∀x (DeadlyDisease(x) → LowSurvivalRate(x)) ::: If something is a deadly disease, then it comes with a low survival rate.
SevereCancer(bileDuctCancer) ::: Severe cancers are deadly diseases.
∀x (Cholangiocarcinoma(x) → bileDuctCancer(x)) ::: All Cholangiocarcinoma is bile duct cancer.
∃x (bileDuctCancer(x)) ::: Bile duct cancer exists.
∃x (Cholangiocarcinoma(x)) ::: Cholangiocarcinoma exists.
MildFlu comes with a low survival rate ::: Mild flu comes with a low survival rate.
¬(bileDuctCancer(colorectalCancer) ∧ LowSurvivalRate(colorectalCancer)) ::: Colorectal cancer is not both a bile duct cancer and with a low survival rate.

Conclusion:
(ColorectalCancer(x) ∧ (bileDuctCancer(x) ∨ Cholangiocarcinoma(x))) → (bileDuctCancer(x) ∧ MildFlu(x))
